name: stone

attributes.attribute: a sign of the divine in a sacred world
roars when the true king sits on it
the royal hill of the high king's inauguration
said to map the four provinces of Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The stone is a mythic motif. The old people of Ireland, Britain, and Brittany were skilled stonemasons. They raised works of stone that have now stood near six thousand years. They also cut their signs into the rock. The Celts, who came to those lands much later, did not carve stone in that deep way. But they took the great sites for their own use. At the royal seat of Tara the stone called the Lia Fáil was said to roar when the true king sat on it. At Ireland's center the Stone of Divisions was said to map the four provinces. The Celts did believe the world was holy. The stone, like the tree and the running water, was a sign that the divine was near.
